name: Watch statistics
description: What was watched, by whom and when, and the top titles, from Jellyfin's Playback Reporting, with no second database.
author: TheMightyTRexUK

settings.label: Leave out these people
settings.hint: One Jellyfin user name a line, such as an account for testing.

changed: **Reaches Starboard on any network:** with Starboard 0.23.0 or later it calls Starboard through a socket in its own folder, so it works on its own closed network too. An older Starboard works as before.
**Clearer words:** **Read the figures again now** is now **Check now**, as on the other plug-ins.
**Logo description:** where its logo stands on its own, a screen reader says "Watch statistics logo", the plug-in's name, instead of a description of the symbol.

fixed: **Jellyfin 12:** it sends Jellyfin's key the way Jellyfin 12 asks for it, so Jellyfin no longer refuses its requests where legacy authorisation is off. Older Jellyfin still works.

changed: **Lighter at rest:** it wakes about once a minute while nothing asks it anything, not twice a second, and writes nothing to its folder when a run goes well.
**Starts faster:** its image comes with Python's modules already compiled, so a start takes about a quarter of the processor time.

added: **A logo** in Settings, Plug-ins, in the Catalogue and on its dashboard cards.
**Its cards say how things are:** a status and when they last changed, in the grey band at the top of each card.
**Updates safely:** before an update it finishes what it is doing and starts nothing new.
changed: Needs Starboard with plug-in API 1.14 or later. A Starboard with an older plug-in API keeps version 1.0.0.

added: **Three tables:** recent plays by day, top titles and people, each to read only, with search and sorting.
**Four cards:** plays this week, top titles, who watched most, and where the figures come from.
Reads Jellyfin's Playback Reporting with one query, so a Full install can go without Jellystat and its PostgreSQL.
Without Playback Reporting it says so and how to add it, and shows each person's last plays from Jellyfin itself.
Rests when not in use, and keeps each answer for 15 minutes.
